# Cleverbrush Framework

> Schema-first TypeScript libraries for validation, HTTP APIs, typed clients,
> database access, forms and object mapping. Libraries compose without codegen.

Start with schemas, share a browser-safe API contract, implement its handlers on
the server, then create a client from that same contract. Database schemas and
public response schemas can differ; select and map fields explicitly.

## Package map

| Area | Package | Documentation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validation and extensions | `@cleverbrush/schema` | [Schema](https://schema.cleverbrush.com) |
| JSON Schema conversion | `@cleverbrush/schema-json` | [README](https://github.com/cleverbrush/framework/tree/development/libs/schema-json) |
| HTTP contracts and handlers | `@cleverbrush/server` | [Server](/server) |
| HTTP clients and React hooks | `@cleverbrush/client` | [Client](/client/getting-started) |
| API specifications | `@cleverbrush/server-openapi` | [OpenAPI / AsyncAPI](/server-openapi) |
| Authentication and authorization | `@cleverbrush/auth` | [Auth](/auth) |
| Dependency injection | `@cleverbrush/di` | [DI](/di) |
| Environment configuration | `@cleverbrush/env` | [Env](/env) |
| SQL queries and schema metadata | `@cleverbrush/knex-schema` | [Queries](/knex-schema) |
| Entities, relations and tracking | `@cleverbrush/orm` | [ORM](/orm) |
| Database migrations | `@cleverbrush/orm-cli` | [README](https://github.com/cleverbrush/framework/tree/development/libs/orm-cli) |
| Object transformations | `@cleverbrush/mapper` | [Mapper](/mapper) |
| Schema-driven React forms | `@cleverbrush/react-form` | [Forms](/react-form) |
| Worker-thread jobs | `@cleverbrush/scheduler` | [Scheduler](/scheduler) |

## Core workflow

This small example uses an in-memory collection, not persistent storage. Keep
`contracts.ts` shared; do not import server implementations into browser bundles.

### 1. Define schemas and the shared contract

```typescript
// contracts.ts
import { defineApi, endpoint } from '@cleverbrush/server/contract';
import { array, boolean, number, object, string } from '@cleverbrush/schema';

export const Todo = object({
    id: number(),
    title: string(),
    completed: boolean()
});
const CreateTodo = object({ title: string().minLength(1).maxLength(200) });

export const api = defineApi({
    todos: {
        list: endpoint.get('/api/todos').responses({ 200: array(Todo) }),
        create: endpoint.post('/api/todos')
            .body(CreateTodo).responses({ 201: Todo })
    }
});
```

### 2. Implement the handlers

```typescript
// todos.ts
import { ActionResult, implement } from '@cleverbrush/server';
import type { InferType } from '@cleverbrush/schema';
import { api, Todo } from './contracts.js';

const rows: InferType<typeof Todo>[] = [];
let nextId = 1;
export const todosModule = implement(api).group('todos').withHandlers({
    list: () => rows,
    create: ({ body }) => {
        const todo = { id: nextId++, title: body.title, completed: false };
        rows.push(todo);
        return ActionResult.created(todo);
    }
});
```

For large APIs, export a configured scope and define each handler in its own file
using `Handler<typeof scope.endpoints.operation>`. Compose feature modules at the
root. See the [multi-file example](https://github.com/cleverbrush/framework/blob/development/libs/server/README.md#large-apis-and-shared-error-handling).

### 3. Register the complete implementation

```typescript
// server.ts
import { createServer, implement } from '@cleverbrush/server';
import { api } from './contracts.js';
import { todosModule } from './todos.js';

const server = createServer().withHealthcheck();
server.handleAll(implement(api).use(todosModule).complete());
await server.listen(3000);
```

`complete()` checks contract coverage. Server request validation and response
types come from the endpoint schemas. Application persistence, permissions and
business rules remain application code.

### 4. Call the API from a typed client

```typescript
// client.ts
import { createClient } from '@cleverbrush/client';
import { timeout } from '@cleverbrush/client/timeout';
import { api } from './contracts.js';

export const client = createClient(api, {
    baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000',
    middlewares: [timeout({ timeout: 10_000 })]
});
const todos = await client.todos.list();
const created = await client.todos.create({ body: { title: 'Buy milk' } });
```

## Schemas and extension authoring

Schemas are immutable. Capture the returned builder when adding properties,
validators or modifiers. `number()` validates integers by default;
`.clearIsInteger()` permits fractional values. Use `.coerce()` explicitly when
parsing strings such as query parameters. `InferType<typeof schema>` derives the
value type. Named schemas and `schemaRef()` support composition across packages.

Define custom methods with `defineExtension()` and apply them with
`withExtensions()`. Metadata is available from `schema.introspect().extensions`.
For metadata-only methods whose values must also survive in TypeScript, use
`defineMetadataMethod(key).argument<T>()`, `.value(value)` or `.compute(fn)` and
`InferExtensionMetadata<S>`. These do not alter global builder prototypes or
interpret application-specific metadata. See [schema extensions](https://github.com/cleverbrush/framework/blob/development/libs/schema/README.md#extensions).

## HTTP APIs and supporting services

- **Server:** endpoint builders describe request schemas, response statuses,
  injection and authorization. `route()` supports schema-typed path parameters.
  `implement()` binds modular handlers; `errorMap()` / `withErrors()` translate
  known exceptions only into responses declared by the endpoint. `ActionResult`
  supplies status-specific, file and streaming results. Unexpected errors retain
  the server's Problem Details handling. [Server reference](/server).
- **Subscriptions:** use `endpoint.subscription()` with `.incoming()` and
  `.outgoing()` schemas and async-generator handlers. Subscriptions participate
  in implementation coverage but do not use HTTP error policies. [Subscriptions](https://github.com/cleverbrush/framework/blob/development/libs/server/README.md#websocket-subscriptions).
- **Client:** `createClient(contract, options)` infers calls from the contract.
  Middleware is imported from subpaths such as `/retry`, `/timeout`, `/dedupe`,
  `/cache` and `/batching`. Authentication, retry and cache policy must match the
  application. The `/react` client adds TanStack Query hooks including
  `.useQuery()` and `.useMutation()`; query state uses `isLoading`.
  `decodeValidationIssues()` extracts structured request-validation issues.
  [Client reference](/client/getting-started).
- **OpenAPI / AsyncAPI:** configure `serveOpenApi({ server, info })` or
  `serveAsyncApi({ server, info })` as middleware before listening. For generation
  without middleware, pass registration metadata to `generateOpenApiSpec()` or
  `generateAsyncApiSpec()`. Named schemas become reusable components.
  [Specification generation](/server-openapi).
- **Authentication:** configure authentication schemes and authorization policies
  on the server; declare endpoint principal requirements with `.authorize()`.
  JWT, cookies, OAuth2 and OIDC are supported. Keep signing keys and server-only
  configuration out of shared contracts. [Authentication](/auth).
- **Dependency injection:** schemas act as typed service tokens. Register values
  or factories with singleton/scoped/transient lifetimes. Endpoint `.inject()`
  declares dependencies supplied as the handler's second argument.
  [Dependency injection](/di).
- **Environment:** `env(name, schema)` binds leaves in a nested configuration;
  `parseEnv()` validates and resolves it. `parseEnvFlat()` supports flat configs.
  Use explicit coercion and `envBoolean()` for environment boolean conventions.
  [Environment configuration](/env).

## Database queries, entities and result mapping

Import database-capable schema factories from `@cleverbrush/knex-schema` or
`@cleverbrush/orm`, not plain `@cleverbrush/schema`. Table and column metadata
belong to these packages. Knex is a peer dependency; PostgreSQL also needs `pg`.

- **Queries:** `query(knex, schema)` / `createQuery(knex)` provide typed selectors,
  CRUD, scopes, named projections, eager loading and transactions. Aliases express
  flat joins; aggregate expressions support summaries and explicit output schemas.
  Composite cursors require a deterministic, non-null sort with a unique
  tie-breaker. [Query guide](/knex-schema).
- **ORM:** `defineEntity(schema)` declares relations; `createDb(knex, entities)`
  exposes typed DbSets. Ordinary entity queries support identity tracking,
  change persistence, optimistic concurrency and STI/CTI variants. Use
  `@cleverbrush/orm-cli` for migrations. [ORM guide](/orm).
- **Projection-aware reads:** enter `.withRowSchema()` before selecting or
  including. It returns an immutable, read-only query. `rowSchema` describes the
  decoded selection, not the full table, and accessing it never executes SQL.
  Results are detached even in tracking contexts. SQL nulls stay `null`, dates
  decode to `Date` throughout nested graphs, and declared decimal/bigint columns
  retain exact strings. Input defaults and preprocessors are not replayed.
  [Read schemas](/knex-schema#row-schemas), [detached ORM reads](/orm#detached-read-schemas).
- **Nested and polymorphic reads:** child customizers return their configured
  queries. Nested includes execute in one SQL statement. STI/CTI readers expose
  a union `rowSchema` and per-variant `variantRowSchemas`; DTO selection and
  discriminator dispatch remain explicit application code.
- **Mapping:** `mapper().configure(Source, Target, configure)` checks that every
  target property is mapped, auto-mapped or ignored. `.from()` copies values;
  `.compute()` transforms them. `getMapper()` returns an asynchronous function.
  `getSyncMapper()` returns ordinary values when all final steps and nested
  mappings are synchronous; known async mappings are rejected and disguised
  thenables throw when invoked. Configuration does not probe callbacks. Reuse
  schema instances and configured mappings; the registry uses schema identity.
  Mapping does not fetch data or authorize access. [Mapper guide](/mapper),
  [synchronous mapping](/mapper#synchronous-mapping).

For separate query, mapping and service files, storage representation rules and
supported read operations, see the [complete query README](https://github.com/cleverbrush/framework/blob/development/libs/knex-schema/README.md#projection-aware-reads).

## Forms and background work

- **React Form:** schema-driven fields, validation and submission state.
  Structured `FormIssue` values carry server validation errors to nested fields;
  application business errors require explicit paths. [Forms](/react-form).
- **Scheduler:** `JobScheduler` runs configured jobs in worker threads with
  scheduling, retry, timeout and lifecycle events. Configure job files and
  timezone explicitly. [Scheduler](/scheduler).
